correctness.rationale: For each proper completion, a part using at least two colours has at most Q-2 distinct neighbour colours, hence must be initially fully seeded. Any first force sees Q-1 outside colours and therefore makes the resulting proper colouring surjective with its own part monochromatic. Two empty monochromatic parts leave no possible first force. Conversely all but at most one monochromatic part seeded allows that empty part to fill, followed by all remaining blanks. This is an exact iff argument for arbitrary parameters. Multinomial palette assignment gives Q! product S(n_i,s_i), correctly handles total non-surjective full colourings separately, and the balanced result follows by capacity and explicit constructions. A direct graph-based enumeration agreed with a separate Stirling computation in 18 finite cases; balanced minimum/multiplicity checked in 16. Finite checks are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Farr establishes the general forcing polynomial, basic used-colour necessity, and lambda=2 bipartite formula; the published complete multipartite formula covers only lambda=r, while the published three-colour biclique formula covers r=2. The present statement is restricted to r>=3 and all Q>r and supplies a complete stronger part-palette classification, an explicit Stirling enumerator, and balanced sharp minimum multiplicities not implied by those narrower results. Actual published-finding corpus claim/alias and web searches found no dominating theorem. Priority remains contingent on unindexed work.
residual_risks: No independent or exhaustive priority survey; unindexed notes or older terminology for forcing partial vertex colourings could contain equivalent formulas.
The stated polynomial is an algebraic consequence of the new classification together with standard Stirling counts; the standard underlying Stirling identities are not new.
Only selected relevant sections of the 29-page Farr paper were read in detail, although the full text was searchable.

value.rationale: The mathematical gap is the forced-colouring probability polynomial above the chromatic palette, which Farr identifies as substantially harder beyond bipartite two-colour cases and which a published complete-multipartite result limits to Q=r. This result gives an exact all-sizes, all-surplus-Q polynomial, a complete characterization of forceable restrictions, and a sharp balance-sensitive staircase with exact extremal multiplicity and an abrupt terminal transition. These are mathematically motivated structural and enumerative results, not just a small count, name change, or standard high-degree obstruction. It resolves the natural previously uncovered palette parameter for an important infinite graph class.
